correctness.rationale: A forced partial bijection has n-k directed paths; completions permute their terminals to their initials, forbid fixed singleton paths, and have sign (-1)^(n-c-t) for t cycles of the path permutation. With at least four free rows the diagonal and forbidden-negative cells form two partial matchings. At four rows the second matching removes at most two cells and cannot kill the three even double transpositions or all six odd four-cycles. At five rows I independently counted both signs for all seven conjugacy types after extension to two full forbidden matchings. At six or more rows two common columns and Hall's theorem give opposite-sign completions by a swap. At rank n-2 only the all-positive and one-negative labels remain. A singleton forces crossing in the all-positive case; cutting a two-vertex path forbids two-cycle completions on the resulting three paths; cutting a cycle with two original singletons imposes the sign opposite that for all positives. Every other cut permits both signs by the three-cycle and a legal transposition. The rank n-3 exception and rank n-1 obstruction follow as stated. Ordering the two directed paths gives n!D_(m,c)/m! arrangements; division by two and parity projection give both top-coefficient formulas. An independent bitset partition of actual even derangements by Boolean traces checked 52,160 supports through n=7, recovering top counts 0, 240, 1140 and 15750; finite replay corroborates but does not replace the all-order argument.
residual_risks: Ordinary incidence shattering of even derangements with n>=4 only; no claim for adaptive shattering or more general boards.
